header: Faisal Hayat Versus The State etc.
body: Appellant by: Ch. Muhammad Akhtar, Advocate.
State by: Syed Zaheer Abbas Shah, ADPP with Sadaqat SI.
Complainant by: Mian Abdul Rauf, Advocate.

SADAQAT ALI KHAN, J. Appellant (Faisal Hayat) alongwith his co-accused Arif Imran and Tariq Noor (since acquitted) has been tried by the trial Court in case FIR No.232 dated 05.05.2024 in offences under Sections 302/109 PPC Police Station Pindigheb, District Attock, and was convicted and sentenced vide judgement dated 30.09.2026 as under:- Faisal Hayat (Appellant)

u/s 302 (b) PPC Sentenced to DEATH as Ta’zir for committing Qatl-i-Amd of Azhar Mehmood (deceased) with compensation of Rs.500,000/payable to legal heirs of deceased u/s 544-A Cr.P.C. and in default whereof to further undergo simple imprisonment for 6-months.

2. Appellant has filed this Criminal Appeal against his conviction and the trial Court has sent Murder Reference for confirmation of his death sentence or otherwise, which are being decided through this single judgment.
3. Heard. Record perused.

4. Azhar Mehmood sustained firearm injuries at the hands of appellant during the occurrence took place in front of Tayyab Karyana Store on 05.05.2024 at about 09:00 p.m. whereafter FIR was lodged on the same night at 10:50 p.m. on the statement of his brother Farhat Abbas PW-14 who being eyewitness while appearing before the trial Court stated in his statement as under:- “On 05.05.2024, I alongwith my other brother Azhar Mehmood and Tariq PW went to the shop of Tayyab Karyana Store for purchase of commodities and reached there at about 09:00 pm. Faisal Hayat (accused present in the Court) was already present there who asked my deceased brother Azhar Mehmood not to interfere in the land dispute Shoukat Hayat, Tariq Noor and Arif Imran. Due to this, an altercation took place between Faisal Hayat and Azhar Mehmood. Accused Faisal Hayat took out his pistol from his dub and fired upon Azhar Hayat which hit on his neck. He further fired upon Azhar Mehmood hitting on different parts of his body. Azhar Mehmood fell on receiving fire shot. Faisal Hayat accused while brandishing the pistol fled away from the spot. The occurrence was witnessed by me and Tariq PWs.

Motive behind the occurrence that there was dispute land between Tariq Mehmood, Arif and Shoukat Hayat. Faisal Hayat accused is brother-in-law (sala) of Tariq Mehmood whereas Azhar Mehmood is friend of Shoukat Hayat. On the asking of Tariq Noor and Arif Imran, accused Faisal Hayat fired upon my brother Azhar Mehmood.”
5. Tariq PW-15 being eyewitness of the occurrence has reiterated the same story before the trial Court.
6. Azhar Mehmood (deceased), the then injured, died on 06.05.2024 at 01:45 a.m. (night) after 4 hours and 45 minutes of the occurrence.

7. Azhar Mehmood (deceased), the then injured, after sustaining firearm injuries was brought in THQ Hospital Pindi Gheb. Zameer Hassan, Constable PW-11 present there, got recorded his video statement(s) through his own VIVO mobile phone. Whereafter, said mobile phone was handed over to I.O. which was taken into possession and sent to Punjab Forensic Science Agency for analysis as to whether video statement (s) of Azhar Mehmood, (deceased), the then injured, are genuine, dubbed, mixed, edited or otherwise. After analysis it has been observed as under:- Result(s) and Conclusion(s):
• After forensic video analysis, no editing features were observed in the visual contents of all the video files mentioned above contained in Item#1.

• After forensic audio analysis, no traces of editing were detected in the audio contents of all the video files mentioned above contained in Item # 1 on the basis of tests performed (Binary analysis, Codec tracing analysis, Detection of amplification, Detection of sampling rate manipulation, Copy-Paste forgery detection, and Detection of traces of different recording devices).

8. It is by now well settled that evidence recorded through modern devices is admissible in prevailing law of evidence. Article 164 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 invests the Court with wide powers to allow the production of any evidence that has become available because of modern devices and techniques. The procedure for receiving such evidence has been further smoothened by Articles 46-A and 78-A of the Order and by the Electronic Transactions Ordinance, 2002. The principles for proving an audio or video recording were authoritatively settled in (Ishtiaq Ahmed Mirza and 2 others v. Federation of Pakistan and others (PLD 2019 SC 675): the recording must be shown to be genuine and untampered; the person who made it must be produced, it must be played in court; and the voices or persons depicted must be properly identified. A forensic report confirming that the recording has not been edited or doctored is the surest means of establishing genuineness. Tested against these principles, the video recording of the dying declaration of the deceased in the present case stands on firm ground. It was recorded by Zamir Hassan , who being maker of the video statement(s)

appeared before the trial Court, produced the recording himself, identified the deceased, the then injured, and the circumstances in which the statement was made, and was subjected to cross-examination on its authenticity but could not be shaken. The report of PFSA qua video statement(s) of Azhar Mehmood (deceased), the then injured is positive which[video statement(s)] has been displayed in open court during statement of Zamir Hassan/C . Objection has not been raised by the defence that Azhar Mehmood (deceased), the then injured, was not conscious at the time of recording of his video statement(s). During trial in open Court, video statement(s) of Azhar Mehmood (deceased), the then injured, had been displayed but no objection has been raised that Azhar Mehmood (deceased), the then injured was not making his statement(s) or the person who made statement(s) is not identifiable. It has also not been challenged by the defence that Azhar Mehmood (deceased) the then injured, has not nominated appellant in his video statement(s). In view of above interpolation, substitution or editing of forensic material, seemingly immune from human interference, could not have been possibly manipulated and thus constitutes a piece of evidence that too formidable to be shaken through a bald assertion alone rather without any corroboration such like video statement(s) of the deceased, the then injured, alone is sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused.

9. Zamir Hassan, Constable maker of the video statement(s) of Azhar Mehmood (deceased), the then injured is neither related to complainant nor appellant. He did his job being independent/official witness. Considering above, we are of the view that Azhar Mehmood (deceased), the then injured, has fully implicated the appellant in his video statement(s) as sole perpetrator of the occurrence which statement(s) has rightly been accepted by the trial Court as dying declaration of Azhar Mehmood (deceased), the then injured.

10. Eyewitnesses discussed above have also fully implicated the appellant with effective role of firing on the person of the deceased. They were cross-examined at length but their evidence could not be shaken during the process of cross-examination. They have also established their presence at the time of occurrence at the place of occurrence with their stated reasons. They have corroborated each other on all material aspects of the case. Their evidence is straightforward, trustworthy, confidence inspiring and cannot be discarded mere on probabilities.

11. The discrepancies in the statements of the PWs pointed out by learned counsel for the appellant, are minors and general in nature, occur in every case when witnesses (who are human-being) are cross-examined after a long time of the occurrence as in present case and are not fatal to the prosecution case.

12. Parties were previously known to each other, so there is no question of misidentity of the appellant leaving the actual culprit scot free despite that occurrence took place in the dark hours of the night.
13. Acquittal of co-accused (Arif Imran and Tariq Noor) with different role is also not fatal to the prosecution case. (2020 SCMR 1414) “Javed Ishfaq Vs. The State”.

14. Medical evidence has been furnished by Dr. Ali Hassan Shah PW-10 who during medical examination of Azhar Hayat (deceased, the then injured) provided first aid to him, on his death, Dr. Adnan Arif PW-9 during post-mortem examination on the dead body of Azhar Hayat observed firearm injuries on his person attributed to the appellant, which were ante-mortem in nature and were sufficient to cause death in ordinary course of nature, therefore, medical evidence has fully supported the ocular account discussed above.

15. Motive of the occurrence was an altercation took place between the appellant and Azhar Mehmood, deceased on the dispute of land between Shaukat Hayat (friend of deceased) and Tariq Noor and Arif Imran (co-accused since acquitted) but solid evidence qua the altercation between appellant and the deceased has not been produced which is not believable.
16. Pistol .9-MM recovered on pointing out of the appellant has matched with the crime empties collected from the place of occurrence.

17. Appellant has denied his involvement in this case in his statement recorded u/s 342 Cr.P.C. and stated that he is innocent and has falsely been involved in this case. He has neither opted to appear u/s 340 (2) Cr.P.C. nor produced defence evidence except certain documents in support of his defence plea which is not believable.

18. In view of above, if evidence of motive is excluded from consideration, even then prosecution has proved its case beyond shadow of doubt against the appellant through the evidence discussed earlier.

19. Coming to the quantum of sentence, we have noted some mitigating circumstances i.e. firstly co-accused (Arif Imran and Tariq Noor) have been acquitted by the learned trial Court vide impugned judgement and secondly, motive story has been disbelieved by us with the reasons mentioned in Para 15 of this judgment. It is not determinable in this case as to what was the real cause of occurrence and as to what had actually happened immediately before the occurrence which resulted into present unfortunate incident. (2014 SCMR 1227) “Zafar Iqbal and others Vs. The State”.

20. Considering above, while maintaining the conviction of the appellant (Faisal Hayat) in offence under Section 302(b) PPC, his sentence is altered from death to imprisonment for life. The compensation and sentence in default whereof awarded by the trial Court are also maintained. Benefit of Section 382-B Cr.P.C. is extended to the appellant.

21. Consequently, with the above said modification in the impugned judgment, instant Criminal Appeal filed by the appellant (Faisal Hayat) is hereby dismissed. Murder Reference is answered in NEGATIVE and death sentence of Faisal Hayat (appellant) is NOT CONFIRMED. (SYED FARHAD ALI SHAH)
Judge (SADAQAT ALI KHAN)
